title: US Charity Deploys AI to Scan for Hate in Gaza Classrooms
summary:
The Gaza Children Village is installing audio monitoring equipment in its schools to identify inciting or antisemitic comments among students and staff. The U.S. charity will use artificial intelligence to analyze recordings of conversations for thousands of children to ensure teachers adhere to a peace-focused curriculum, with alerts for questionable content sent directly to the founder.

Audio files will be stored for 72 hours, though individuals affiliated with the charity have voiced concerns regarding free speech and privacy. These monitored lessons are currently conducted in tents and under tarp coverings, as Israeli forces destroyed previous school buildings and blocked the reconstruction of permanent facilities.

🇺🇸🇵🇸 A U.S. charity wants to put AI in Gaza's classrooms to monitor what teachers and students say, flagging anything it considers hateful or antisemitic.

Gaza Children Village runs schools for thousands of children affected by the war, providing education, food and medical care. 

Its founder says the goal is to promote peace and tolerance, partly by removing material he believes encourages hatred of Israel.

Now he wants classroom conversations recorded and scanned by AI, with alerts sent directly to him when the system catches something questionable.

The recordings would reportedly be kept for 72 hours, but even people connected to the charity are raising privacy and free-speech concerns. 

The charity says it's about making sure the curriculum is followed. 

Fair enough, but who decides what counts as hateful speech, especially when AI is doing the listening?

Source: AP / Writer: Julie
